subtype_info: actinomycetoma of the lower limb diagnosed with dermoscopy-guided biopsy
title: Dermoscopy aids in lesion selection for microbiological and histopathological assessment of mycetoma
case_text: A 62-year-old man presented to the dermatology clinic with skin lesions that erupted 2 years ago and had been progressing since then. He had reported pus-like discharge that sometimes contained particles from some of his skin lesions. On examination, the left lower limb showed remarkable swelling. There were multiple hyperpigmented, indurated nodules over the left thigh and knee [Figure 1a]. A dermoscopy-unguided punch skin biopsy was obtained; it revealed only scarring but no diagnostic findings. All lesions were examined using a dermoscope (DermLite DL II Hybrid; 3 Gen Inc.) to aid in the selection of more potentially diagnostic sampling sites. Two types of lesions were identified: The first exhibited central erythema surrounded by a palisade of radial white lines indicating fibrosis [Figure 1b and c] and the second revealed a central zone exhibiting an erosion and variable-sized white globules surrounded by an interrupted fringe of white scales with a peripheral palisade of radiating white lines indicative of fibrosis [Figure 1d and e]. Lesional puncture resulted in extrusion of either serosanguinous discharge [Figure 1b] or numerous white grains dispersed in purulent exudate [Figure 2a]. The grains were sent to the laboratory for Gram staining. An intact lesion showing white grains on dermoscopy was biopsied and stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H and E), periodic acid-Schiff (PAS), and Grocott methenamine silver (GMS) stains. Gram-stained smears demonstrated Gram-positive filamentous bacteria [Figure 2b]. Histopathologic sections showed grains within an area of suppurative granulomatous dermatitis on H&E [Figure 2c], but no positivity to PAS or GMS. Sanger sequencing and BLAST alignment identified 100% sequence identity with streptomyces sp., but no fungal DNA was detected. A diagnosis of actinomycetoma was made and the patient was commenced on treatment accordingly.
